quests.correctAnswer: The task of constructing a normative theory adequate to the unprecedented ethical challenges posed by the development of transformative technologies including artificial intelligence biotechnology and synthetic biology requires not only technical expertise but philosophical imagination historical perspective and moral courage.

quests.correctAnswer: She argued that the widespread acceptance of the public-private partnership model as the preferred modality of infrastructure provision in developing countries reflected ideological commitments to market efficiency that were impervious to a substantial body of empirical evidence suggesting the superiority of alternative institutional arrangements in many contexts.

quests.correctAnswer: He contended that the contemporary crisis of liberal democracy was best understood not as a failure of the democratic ideal itself but as the consequence of a long process of institutional hollowing-out in which the formal procedures of democracy had been progressively decoupled from the substantive conditions that gave them their legitimating force.

quests.correctAnswer: The profound philosophical difficulty in formulating a coherent account of global distributive justice that is simultaneously theoretically robust politically feasible and responsive to the extraordinary diversity of circumstances and values across the world's cultures and political traditions has led many theorists to conclude that the entire enterprise is fundamentally misconceived.

quests.correctAnswer: She maintained that the emergence of what she termed the attention economy in which the finite cognitive resources of human beings had been systematically colonised by profit-maximising platforms in ways that undermined both individual autonomy and the quality of public deliberation represented a form of harm that existing regulatory frameworks were wholly unprepared to address.

quests.correctAnswer: She contended that the analytical distinction between empirical and normative political theory while methodologically useful had increasingly become a site of ideological contestation in which claims to scientific objectivity functioned not to insulate political science from normative commitments but to naturalise and depoliticise particular configurations of political power.

quests.correctAnswer: He argued that the intellectual failure of the development economics profession to anticipate explain or provide effective remedies for the persistent gap between the development potential of low-income countries and their actual developmental trajectories reflected fundamental limitations in the theoretical frameworks and methodological tools through which those trajectories had been analysed.

quests.correctAnswer: The historical evidence strongly suggests that periods of hegemonic transition in the international system those moments when rising powers challenge and ultimately displace established hegemons are among the most dangerous phases of international history generating levels of systemic instability that increase significantly the risk of major conflict.

quests.correctAnswer: He contended that the growing body of empirical research on the determinants of democratic backsliding which consistently identified executive aggrandisement partisan polarisation and the erosion of independent judicial and media institutions as the primary pathways through which democracies declined had fundamentally transformed scholars' understanding of how democratic systems failed.

quests.correctAnswer: Whether the trajectory of technological development is best understood as an autonomous force operating according to its own internal logic as a neutral tool shaped entirely by the social forces that deploy it or as a constitutively political phenomenon that simultaneously reflects and transforms the power relations within which it is developed represents a fundamental question at the intersection of philosophy of technology and political sociology.

quests.correctAnswer: He observed that the history of successful social movements demonstrated that the relationship between structural conditions ideological innovation organisational capacity and political opportunity was so complex and contingent that no general theory of social change could do justice to the range of historically specific pathways through which fundamental transformations had actually been achieved.

quests.correctAnswer: The central paradox of technological modernity lies in the fact that the same processes of rationalisation standardisation and efficiency-optimisation that have made possible unprecedented levels of human welfare and capability have simultaneously created new forms of alienation vulnerability and existential risk that earlier generations could not have imagined.

quests.correctAnswer: She argued that the most intellectually honest response to the genuine difficulties of theorising global justice was neither to abandon the enterprise in favour of a resigned acceptance of the existing order nor to proceed as if those difficulties were merely technical problems that would yield to further theoretical refinement but rather to treat them as permanent features of the political and philosophical landscape that demanded ongoing negotiation.

quests.correctAnswer: He contended that the most significant intellectual development in the study of comparative politics over the past two decades had been the gradual displacement of structural and institutional approaches by more agency-centred accounts that took seriously the strategic calculations normative commitments and creative improvisations of political actors operating under conditions of uncertainty.

quests.correctAnswer: The extraordinary concentration of epistemic authority in the hands of a small number of globally dominant knowledge-producing institutions universities think tanks journals and funding bodies located overwhelmingly in the global North raises fundamental questions about whose knowledge counts whose experiences are theorised and whose problems are deemed worthy of sustained intellectual attention.

quests.correctAnswer: He argued that the most important and underappreciated insight of the pragmatist tradition in American philosophy was its insistence that the sharp distinction between theory and practice between knowledge and action and between the descriptive and the normative was not merely philosophically untenable but practically harmful insofar as it had licensed the cultivation of theoretical sophistication at the expense of practical wisdom.
